title: A 400-pound stranger convinced a grieving mother he was her drowned son. How?
description:
In 1866, a 27-stone butcher from Wagga Wagga arrived in London claiming to be Sir Roger Tichborne, heir to a fortune. Roger had drowned in 1854 when the Bella sank off Brazil. This man had no tattoo, couldn't speak French, and didn't recognize his own horse. But Roger's grieving mother looked at him once and said, "This is my son."

Servants who knew Roger for decades were horrified. Investigators identified the claimant as Arthur Orton, a butcher's son from Wapping. A civil trial in 1871 ran 103 days — the longest in English legal history. He lost, was arrested for perjury, convicted after a second 188-day trial, and sentenced to 14 years' hard labor.

He served ten years, sold a confession to a newspaper, recanted it four days later, and died in 1898 still signing letters "Sir Roger Tichborne." His coffin bore the name he went to prison for stealing.
